meta.title: Bootlift: Spring Boot 4 readiness check for pull requests
meta.description: Open-source GitHub Action that scores Spring Boot 4 readiness, blocks new migration debt in pull requests and suggests one-click fixes. No JDK, no build.

hero.title: Upgrade to Spring Boot 4 without the migration debt.
hero.subtitle: Bootlift scores Spring Boot 4 readiness on every pull request, fails only on the lines you add, and turns fixes into one-click suggestions. In seconds, with no JDK and no build.

footer.tagline: Spring Boot 4 readiness, checked on every pull request.

whyNow.title: Spring Boot 4 moves the ground under your code.
whyNow.intro: Boot 4 adopts Jakarta EE 11 and Jackson 3, removes @MockBean and renames 96 configuration properties. Bootlift finds each of them before the upgrade does.

how.title: Three steps, on every pull request.
how.intro: Bootlift runs as one step in your workflow. Nothing to install on the runner, nothing to configure.

scan.title: Scan
scan.body: Reads build files, configuration and Java or Kotlin code as plain text. Nothing is compiled and no JDK is installed.

score.title: Score
score.body: Every finding weighs on a 0 to 100 readiness score. You get one PR comment, updated on each push, plus the job summary and annotations on the lines.

guard.title: Guardrail and suggestions
guard.body: In pull requests only added lines can fail the job. Legacy code counts in the score but never blocks anyone. Fixes with a certain answer arrive as one-click suggestions.

how.legacyNote: Counts in the score. Never blocks.
how.addedNote: Can fail the job. Comes with a suggestion.

demo.intro: bootlift-demo scores 94 on main. A pull request with old code drops it to 60 and fails with 6 suggestions. Applying them brings it back to 94, green. The demo repository is written in Portuguese.

rules.title: 12 rules, each with a way out.
rules.intro: Checked in code, build files and configuration. Four of them fix themselves with one click.

items.BOOT_VERSION: Spring Boot below 3.5 (warning), or on 3.5.x and ready for 4.0 (info).
items.JAVA_BASELINE: Java below 17. Boot 4 requires 17 or newer.
items.GRADLE_VERSION: Gradle wrapper below 8.14, the minimum for the Boot 4 plugin.
items.JAKARTA_NAMESPACE: Jakarta EE imports still on javax.*, such as servlet and persistence.
items.JACKSON3_NAMESPACE: Jackson 2 packages. Boot 4 uses Jackson 3 (tools.jackson); annotations stay where they are.
items.MOCKBEAN_REMOVED: @MockBean and @SpyBean were removed in favour of @MockitoBean and @MockitoSpyBean.
items.UNDERTOW_REMOVED: Undertow was removed: it is not yet compatible with Servlet 6.1.
items.SPOCK_REMOVED: The Spock integration left Boot 4.0. The Spring team announced its return in 4.1.
items.SESSION_REMOVED: Boot no longer configures Spring Session for MongoDB or Hazelcast.
items.STARTER_RENAMED: Renamed starters: web → webmvc, aop → aspectj, oauth2-* → security-oauth2-* and others.
items.LAUNCH_SCRIPT: The launch script for executable jars was removed.
items.PROPERTY_RENAMED: 96 renamed properties in application.*, YAML and .properties.

afterNotes.SESSION_REMOVED: Redis or JDBC, or the project's own module

quickstart.title: Add it in one step.
quickstart.intro: Save this workflow in your repository, for example as .github/workflows/bootlift.yml. The next pull request gets a score, a report and suggestions.

inputDesc.path: Root of the project to analyze.
inputDesc.mode: guardrail or full. Empty means guardrail on pull_request and full on other events.
inputDesc.fail-on: Lowest severity that fails the job: none, warning or error.
inputDesc.comment-on-pr: Posts or updates the report comment on the PR.
inputDesc.suggestions: In guardrail mode, posts each deterministic fix as a one-click suggestion.
inputDesc.github-token: Token to read the PR diff and comment. On fork PRs it is read-only and the action only warns.

outputDesc.score: Readiness score from 0 to 100 for the whole repository.
outputDesc.blocking: Findings that can fail the job in the current mode.
outputDesc.errors: Findings with error severity in the whole repository.

permDesc.contents: Read the repository code. actions/checkout already asks for it.
permDesc.pr: Read the PR diff, comment and post suggestions. Without it the report still goes to the job summary.

quickstart.v1: Follows every 1.x release: fixes and new rules arrive on their own.
quickstart.vExact: Pins this exact release. You update it by hand.

score.title: How the score is counted.
score.intro: It starts at 100. Each rule found subtracts its severity weight once, plus 1 for every extra occurrence, up to 10 more per rule. It never goes below 0.
score.note: Thirty javax imports weigh as one big problem, not thirty.

fork.q: Does it work on pull requests from forks?
fork.a: The report does: score, job summary, annotations and fail-on all work. One-click suggestions don't, because the token on fork pull requests is read-only.

noise.q: Will it flood a legacy repository with comments?
noise.a: No. It keeps one comment, updated on every push. In guardrail mode legacy findings appear collapsed in that comment and only count in the score; suggestions go only on added lines, at most 20 per review.

monorepo.a: Point path at one service and run the action once per service, for example with strategy.matrix.

falsePositive.q: I found a false positive. Now what?
falsePositive.a: Open the false-positive form with the file and the line. The analysis works line by line, so an import or annotation split across lines can slip through too.

jdk.q: Do I need a JDK or a build?
jdk.a: No. Bootlift reads files as text, so it runs in seconds without installing Java or compiling anything.

cost.a: Nothing. It's free and open source under the MIT license.

finalCta.title: Merge the next PR without new migration debt.
finalCta.body: One step in your workflow. Every pull request after it is checked against Spring Boot 4.
